'''''Celosia''''' ({{IPAc-en|s|iː|ˈ|l|oʊ|ʃ|i|ə}} {{respell|see|LOH|shee|ə}}<ref>{{cite book|title=Sunset Western Garden Book|year=1995|pages=606–607}}</ref>) is a small genus of edible and [[ornamental plant]]s in the [[amaranth]] family, [[Amaranthaceae]]. Its species are commonly known as '''woolflowers''', or, if the flower heads are crested by [[fasciation]], '''cockscombs'''.<ref>{{cite EB1911|wstitle=Cock's-comb|volume=6|page=628}}</ref> The plants are well known in [[East Africa]]'s highlands and are used under their [[Swahili language|Swahili]] name, {{lang|sw|mfungu}}.

== Taxonomy ==
The generic name is derived from the [[Ancient Greek]] word {{lang|grc|κήλεος}} ({{transliteration|grc|kḗleos}}), meaning "burning",<ref>{{LSJ|kh/leos|κήλεος|ref}}</ref> and refers to the colourful flame-like [[Head (botany)|flower heads]].<ref name="MBG">{{cite web |title=''Celosia argentea'' (Plumosa Group) 'New Look' |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=267315 |website=Plant Finder |date=n.d. |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=4 January 2023 }}</ref>

== Uses ==
=== As a garden plant ===
The plant is an [[Annual plant|annual]]. Seed production in these species can be very high, 200–700 kg per hectare.  One ounce of seed may contain up to 43,000 seeds. One thousand seeds can weigh 1.0–1.2 grams.  Depending upon the location and fertility of the soil, blossoms can last 8–10 weeks.{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}

''[[Celosia argentea|C. argentea]]'' and ''[[Celosia cristata|C. cristata]]'' are common garden ornamental plants.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celosia argentea |url=https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/1/7/1794 |access-date=2023-04-06 |website=www.nparks.gov.sg}}</ref>

=== As food ===
''[[Celosia argentea]]'' var. ''argentea'' or Lagos spinach (a.k.a. quail grass, soko, celosia, feather cockscomb) is a broadleaf annual [[leaf vegetable]].  It grows widespread across Mexico, where it is known as "velvet flower", northern South America, tropical Africa, the West Indies, South, East and Southeast Asia where it is grown as a native or naturalized wildflower, and is cultivated as a nutritious leafy green vegetable.  It is traditional fare in the countries of Central and West Africa, and is one of the leading leafy green vegetables in Nigeria, where it is known as "{{lang|yo|soko yokoto}}", meaning "make husbands fat and happy".<ref>{{cite web |last=Yarger |first=Larry |title=Lagos Spinach |url=https://c.ymcdn.com/sites/echocommunity.site-ym.com/resource/collection/d9d576a1-771a-4d95-a889-4fbd9e75d03d/Lagos_Spinach.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118035214/https://c.ymcdn.com/sites/echocommunity.site-ym.com/resource/collection/d9d576a1-771a-4d95-a889-4fbd9e75d03d/Lagos_Spinach.pdf |archive-date=18 January 2017 |url-status=dead |website=ECHO |access-date=2 February 2023}}</ref> In Spain it is known as "Rooster comb" because of its appearance.{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}

As a grain, ''Celosia'' is a [[pseudo-cereal]], not a true [[cereal]].{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}

These leaves, young stems and young inflorescences are used for stew, as they soften up readily in cooking. The leaves also have a soft texture and a mild spinach-like taste.{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}

==Cultivation==

[[File:Silver Cockscomb (Celosia argentea) in Tirunelveli.jpg|right|thumb|Silver cockscomb ''Celosia argentea'' in [[Tirunelveli]], India]]

Despite its African origin (a claim that is not without dispute), ''Celosia'' is known as a foodstuff in Indonesia and India. Moreover, in the future it might become more widely eaten, especially in the hot and malnourished regions of the equatorial zone. In that regard, it has already been hailed as the often-wished-for vegetable that "grows like a weed without demanding all the tender loving care that other vegetables seem to need".<ref>{{cite book |title=Lost Crops of Africa |url=http://books.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=11763&page=94 |year=2006 |volume=II: Vegetables |location=Washington, D.C, USA |publisher=The National Academies Press |isbn=978-0-309-10333-6 |page=94| doi=10.17226/11763 }}</ref>

Works well in humid areas and is the most-used leafy plant in Nigeria. It grows in the wet season and grows well while other plants succumb to mold and other diseases like mildew. Though a very simple plant, ''Celosia'' does need moderate soil moisture.{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}

==Cultural symbolism==
The genus ''Celosia'' is also recognized as an important cultural symbol in [[Cebu]], [[Philippines]]. The local government of [[Cebu City]], together with Sinulog Foundation Incorporated (SFI), declared the Celosia flower as the official flower of the [[Sinulog Festival]], the grandest festival in the Philippines held in honor of [[Santo Niño de Cebu|Santo Niño]] every third Sunday of January. The reason for the move was that the flowers' colors, which are predominantly red and yellow, resemble the colors of the cape, crown, and other regalia of the [[Infant Jesus]]. ''[[Celosia argentea]]'' flowers are still grown seasonally in Sirao Garden, located Barangay Sirao, Cebu City.
